assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishes, through photo-triggered kinetics on ruthenium-modified proteins, how electrons tunnel over long distances through the protein medium, with rates governed by distance and the intervening structure. This is the physical-mechanism framing I value most: it underlies respiration, photosynthesis and redox enzymes, including the electron-transfer steps in the enzymes I study, and it is conceptually clean and foundational.
assessment.attribution: Gray and Winkler are the experimental core and are a compact two-person configuration. Marcus theory was already recognised in 1992, and theoretical pathway models (other groups, not in the credited list) shaped the interpretation, so the split between experiment and theory needs care.
assessment.maturity: Work spans decades, with extensive independent confirmation and incorporation into textbooks and bioenergetics. Recognition is mature, arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Contribution of the theoretical pathway models relative to the experimental work is not on this candidate's credit list.
I recall but have not verified the full priority history of the early ruthenium-protein experiments.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography with X-ray free-electron lasers gives diffraction before radiation damage, enabling room-temperature structures from microcrystals and time-resolved molecular movies of reactions, including membrane proteins and photosynthetic complexes. It makes dynamic mechanisms visible, which I regard as a major methodological advance.
assessment.attribution: Hajdu proposed the diffraction-before-destruction principle, Chapman led the first demonstrations and methods, and Fromme drove the membrane-protein and photosystem applications. Schlichting and others made major time-resolved contributions, so the three-laureate cap makes allocation genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Methods are established and reproduced at several facilities; the time-resolved applications are still developing and some mechanistic claims are not yet settled. Recognition is reasonable but could still be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among Chapman, Hajdu, Fromme, Schlichting and the wider XFEL community is unresolved.
Whether the impact of time-resolved studies on chemical mechanism is sufficiently proven.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural and mechanistic work on nitrogenase explains how N2 is reduced to ammonia at the FeMo cofactor, including its architecture, the central carbide, and the catalytic cycle. It is a fundamental enzymatic mechanism of global biogeochemical importance, handled with spectroscopy, kinetics and crystallography.
assessment.attribution: Rees solved the first structures and the cofactor environment, Einsle identified the interstitial carbide and later structures, and Seefeldt and Dean provided the kinetic and mechanistic framework; Ribbe contributed biosynthesis. The mechanism is a line of work shared by many people, so the credit is diffuse.
assessment.maturity: The structures are well confirmed, but the detailed mechanism of N2 binding and reduction remains under active debate; recognition is partly premature on the mechanism side.
uncertainties: Mechanism of N2 binding and the hydride intermediates is not fully resolved.
Allocation among Rees, Einsle, Seefeldt, Dean and Ribbe is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Concerted proton-electron transfer is a central concept for enzymes and for artificial photosynthesis and fuel-forming electrocatalysis, linking theory with experiment. It is close to my own research on proton transfer coupled to electron transfer, so I judge it from familiarity, and it is physically well grounded.
assessment.attribution: Meyer introduced early concepts of PCET, Mayer developed the thermochemical framework, Hammes-Schiffer the theory and Nocera the model systems and applications. Priority is spread across a field rather than one discovery, so this is more a line of work than a single attributable breakthrough.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are well established and widely applied; the practical impact on catalysis is still developing. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Credit may extend beyond the three chosen names, in particular to Meyer.
Whether this is a single discovery or an umbrella for several advances.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing, from single-channel DNA translocation to protein-pore engineering and motor-controlled single-strand sequencing, created a new analytical technology that reads biopolymers molecule by molecule and is now used in practice.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Branton and Deamer demonstrated DNA translocation; Bayley engineered pores and detection; Akeson achieved enzyme-controlled ratcheting and sequencing. Priority is sharply contested and exceeds three people.
assessment.maturity: Commercially and scientifically established with many independent users, and the maturity is strong.
uncertainties: The conceptual versus engineering priority between the early translocation work and the sequencing implementation.
Whether the contribution is chemistry or instrumentation and biophysics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors perform programmable single-nucleotide conversion without double-strand breaks, built by fusing deaminases to Cas proteins. This is a broad, chemically conceived tool for genetics and therapy, with first clinical results emerging.
assessment.attribution: Liu's group introduced cytosine and adenine base editors, with Komor and Gaudelli as the lead authors; Nishida and Kondo independently reported a related cytidine-deaminase system. CRISPR-Cas9 was already recognised in 2020, so overlap with it must be weighed.
assessment.maturity: Strong replication and fast adoption, but clinical validation is still early and it builds on an already honoured platform.
uncertainties: Nishida and Kondo's priority relative to Liu's group and the role of early authors Komor and Gaudelli.
Whether it is distinct enough from the 2020 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional heteronuclear NMR and relaxation-dispersion methods give atomic-resolution structures and, crucially, dynamics of large biomolecules and transient states in solution, showing motion that static structures cannot. This is a substantial biophysical advance.
assessment.attribution: Bax and Clore developed triple-resonance and residual-dipolar-coupling methods, and Kay the TROSY-based methyl and relaxation methods for large systems. Wagner and Palmer have strong claims, so a limit of three is hard. Wüthrich's 2002 prize covered the initial structure determination.
assessment.maturity: Methods are widely used and confirmed over decades; the recognition is mature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry keeps non-covalent assemblies intact in the gas phase, showing the stoichiometry, composition and lipid interactions of membrane protein complexes. It brought a new tool to structural biochemistry, including respiratory and ATP-synthesising assemblies.
assessment.attribution: Chait, Robinson and Heck are leading contributors; Loo and Gross have earlier or parallel claims. The question is whether the field is one concept or several developments that came after earlier ESI MS recognition in 2002.
assessment.maturity: Technique is well established and independently reproduced; whether the structural interpretation of gas-phase assemblies reflects solution state has been resolved for many systems but not all.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 prize for electrospray ionisation.
Fair credit among Robinson, Heck, Chait, Loo and Gross.
